source.title: SmoothNets: Optimizing CNN architecture design for differentially private deep learning
source.authors: Nicolas W. Remerscheid; A. Ziller; D. Rueckert; Georgios Kaissis

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates differential-privacy utility using validation accuracy; it does not report training classification error or the training-speed behavior named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-accuracy comparisons for DP-SGD-trained architectures. These are related findings about architecture and private-training utility, but do not measure the training-error or training-speed outcomes in the versions. The text also summarizes component sweeps without per-component numbers or identifiable model conditions; those summaries are not extracted as result rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures best-model validation accuracy under DP-SGD, not training classification error, optimization speed, trainable depth, local minima, or learning-rate stability. Its component observations concern private-training utility. Using Xavier-Glorot initialization without comparing initializations does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: SmoothNet outperforms the tested standard architectures and prior architecture-focused approaches on these benchmarks. The authors acknowledge that the contributing mechanisms remain unresolved; optimization-landscape smoothness is a conjecture.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies DP-SGD utility under privacy constraints and compares architectural choices; the claim versions concern training error, training speed, initialization, or stability outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that width-to-depth ratio, connection type, normalization layer, activation function, and pooling choice affect DP-training performance; it does not give per-setting result values for these component observations.

fits_no_version.finding: At ε = 7.0, SmoothNet's best validation accuracy exceeds all four standard architectures on both datasets: 73.5% on CIFAR-10 and 69.7% on ImageNette in Table 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture affects validation utility under the reported DP-SGD recipes, with SmoothNet outperforming the tested standard architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: The component sweeps qualitatively favor wider models, residual and especially dense connections, group normalization, SELU, and max pooling; they provide no training-error or training-speed comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural components influence DP-SGD validation utility in the studied sweeps.

record.peer_reviewed: Submission to Theory and Practice of Differential Privacy (TPDP) Workshop at ICML 2022
record.problems: The paper reports validation accuracy rather than training error; the table gives each architecture's best model and no uncertainty estimates. Component-sweep outcomes are summarized without per-component numerical results in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately attributable component-sweep rows were extracted: the text summarizes effects across over 100 architectures and more than 6000 experiments without reporting per-component values or conditions.

untested.parts: Training classification error, fitting random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size, regularization, or training duration on training error.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and effects of student overparameterization.
Depth-related training-error degradation, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and special initialization or normalization-free training recipes.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above initial stability thresholds, loss and curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 reports selected best models, not average performance or uncertainty. The qualitative component findings are already declared in rows_left_out. Neither the reported width preference nor normalization benefits test the specific optimization outcomes in V2, V3, or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 fitting, model size and training duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain-network training error versus depth, identity-shortcut effects on training error, and the cited special initialization or normalization-free recipes.
Initialization comparisons for signal propagation, training speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature trajectories, and sharpness during full-batch training.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.
